notes.decision: The chapter heading is displayed in three lines with the chapter number ⲙⲁ̄ (=41) repeated as decorative flanking ornament around the title text. Read in linear sequence: 'Chapter 41. Concerning the tongue of the seas.' I render each line literally as transcribed.
Translated 'sign' — Coptic ϫⲱⲣⲙ̄ 'wink, nod, signal.' Standard idiom ϯ ⲟⲩϫⲱⲣⲙⲉ = 'give a sign/signal.'
Form unclear; possibly ⲁⲩϭⲛ 'they found' or causative-perfect of an action verb. Translated tentatively as a verbal continuation. Flagged for parallels.
Translated 'regions' — possibly Lycopolitan ⲧⲟϣ 'boundary, region, district' in plural with possessive. Context (upper place of all the X) supports a topographic-collective reading.

Translated 'raised them up' — from ⲧⲁϩⲟ 'set up, raise, establish' (Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ) with 3pl object suffix. Fits the sequence: scatter wind upon them → blow upon them → raise them up → wash them forth.

Translated 'washed forth' — Coptic ⲉⲓⲱⲉ 'wash' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. The wind washes/cleanses the elements from the earth into the waters. Preserves the purificatory register dominant in the chapter.

Translated 'the Error and the Answering' — both glossed in accumulated vocabulary. ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ = the Error/wandering principle; ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ = the answering/responding. Together they form the cosmic dyad of negative speech-action — what the three places-of-deceit (water/darkness/fire) emit and what is then driven away.

Translated 'salt' (= ⲙⲗⲁϩ in salt-sense). Although the accumulated glossary has ⲙⲗⲁϩ = 'strife,' the immediate context (gustatory pairing with ⲥⲓⲱⲉ 'bitterness' in line 2; thematic 'salt sea' as cosmic locus of bitterness/saltness as the residual taste of dark waters) confirms the gustatory sense. Manichaean cosmological correspondence pairs salt+bitter as the sea's defining tastes.
Greek loanword αὔξειν 'to grow, increase.' Subject is 'a saltness and a bitterness' (singular agreement loose). 'Grew' preserves the verbal force.

ⲁϥⲱⲟⲩⲟ = 'he cast/disposed' (Lyc. for ⲟⲩⲱ); ⲁϥⲓ̈ⲁⲁϥ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'he washed it forth' (ⲉⲓⲱ 'wash'). The Father of Life cleans the cosmic wheel of its dragon-pollutant. Translated as sequential cosmogonic-purificatory acts.

ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ = ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ 'mingle, blend' (cf. ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ in earlier vocab). With ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'inward' = 'was mingled inward (with the counsels of the sea).' The dragon, expelled from the wheel above, mingles into the sea below.

Greek ἐνθύμησις (cosmic Thought, fem.) here functions as the personified principle that re-collects the dragon. Cf. accumulated entry. Treated as feminine subject ('she') in following verbs ⲥⲁⲩϩϥ̄, ⲁⲥⲧⲁⲝⲣⲁϥ, ⲁⲥⲡⲏⲥⲥⲉ.

Greek πέρας 'limit, boundary, end.' Designates the cosmic-temporal limit/boundary of the sea — the marked outer extent within which the seals of time (moments, hours, days, months, years) are imprinted. ⲡⲣⲓⲣⲁⲥ in line 18 is the same word with metathesis or scribal variation.
Likely Lyc. for ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲟⲩⲧⲙ̄ — 'their core/inward part' (cf. ⲟⲩⲧⲙ̄ 'middle, between'). The seals/zodiac-figures are 'cast forth from their inner part' before being thrown into the sea.

Read as a passive 'he was rained down after [it]' continuing the cloud-and-rain image of line 22. ϩⲣⲁ likely related to ⲍⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ/ϩⲣⲱⲟⲩ 'rain' or to a verb of downpour. Alternative: 'they (impersonal) brought him down after [it].' Confidence moderate.

Lyc. ⲧⲛⲟⲩⲧ — possibly 'firmness, solidity' (qualitative of ⲛⲟⲩⲧ 'be hard'); refers here to the 'firm place' (= firmament/established ground) where the dragon is fixed in the establishing of the cosmos.
ⲣ̄-ⲁⲧⲉ unclear; possibly 'became X to him' or 'made herself X for him.' Translated tentatively as 'became' awaiting parallels.

Greek ἀρχιζωγράφος (chief-image-painter) and ἀρχιτέκτων (chief-architect). The sea functions as both painter and master-builder for the dragon's encosmic shape — the cosmological motif of Matter/Hyle as ⲧⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁⲫⲟⲥ (in glossary) here amplified with 'arch-' titles.

Probably Greek-derived for monēsis/coinage-stamping or related metallurgical term — 'coin-dies, mintings.' Context (with ⲡⲧⲁⲃⲉϥ 'mold/seal' and ϩⲟⲗⲟⲕⲟⲧⲓⲛⲟⲥ 'gold solidi') confirms the technical numismatic-metallurgical register.
Read as Lyc. for ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲟ 'the great/many ones' (plural of ⲛⲁⲟ 'great'). Translated 'the many' fitting the sense 'many seals + many forms = one body.'

Translated 'prow' (Greek πρῷρα/πρῖρα). The diaeresis on the iota (ⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲣⲁⲥ) and the masculine -ⲁⲥ ending suggest a Greek loanword; πρῷρα 'ship's prow' fits the cosmological context where this structure (a) functions as a barrier holding things down, (b) blows breath that draws material to itself (lines 27-28). Alternative readings πέρας 'limit, boundary' or πύρρα are possible. Functions as the cosmic prow/boundary of the sea-vessel.
Translated 'they brought it forth' following the accumulated vocabulary entry ϩⲱⲣⲡⲁⲫⲉ/ⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁϥⲉ 'to bring forth/produce.' Here functions as the cosmogonic verb of establishing a structure.
'The residue of the wheel of the sphere.' ⲡⲥⲉⲧⲧⲉ from glossary 'remainder/residue.' This residue is what the prow's purifying function targets.

'Places of dispersion/scattering.' Compound ⲙⲁ-ⲛ-ⲝⲟⲟⲣⲉ where ⲝⲟⲟⲣⲉ = Sahidic ϫⲱⲱⲣⲉ 'scatter, disperse.' The 'three places of dispersion' likely refers to the three earths where archonic abortions are bound — in parallel with the ten firmaments mentioned just before.

Translated 'fastening' as functional rendering. Hapax in this corpus. Context (lines 11, 14) makes the cosmological function clear: a metallic restraining device that, paired with ⲫⲩⲗⲁⲕⲏ 'guard/prison,' holds the wheel and zodiac-signs from rising upward; described in line 14 as 'an iron fastening.' Possible analyses: (a) ⲟⲩⲱϣⲛ̄- + ϥⲧⲟⲩ 'four' = 'four-fold restraint'; (b) related to ⲱϣⲛ̄ 'shut, close.' Etymology uncertain; flagged for parallel research.

Translated 'this peg/nail' from ⲉⲓϣⲉ 'nail, peg' (cf. Crum 86b). The peg is described as 'fastened (ⲉⲧⲁϥⲧ̄ qualitative) into the wheel which is upon the [stake] of the firmaments' — the cosmological pin that holds the wheel in place.
'Her watchers/guards.' Plural of ⲍⲟⲩⲣⲓⲧ 'guard/watcher' (in glossary) with feminine possessive. Identified with the ⲛ̄ⲁⲧⲛ̄ⲕⲁⲧⲉ 'unsleeping ones' — the cosmic Watchers placed over the sphere.

Translated 'transformation/metarrismos' (Greek-derived). Likely μεταρρυθμισμός 'rearrangement, refashioning' or μεταρρευσμός 'change-flow.' Listed alongside ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ 'the Error' as a cosmic flux that descends into the sea. Compare ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'exchange' in glossary as a related Greek-loan abstract.

Translated 'shall serve as the pandocheion (all-receiver).' Greek πανδοχεῖον/πανδοκεῖον 'all-receiving inn, common receptacle' — Lycopolitan with ⲧ for ⲇ and possible scribal metathesis. The sea is identified as the cosmic receptacle that gathers all flowing waters, fire, error, and transformation.
'The place-of-gathering inward.' ⲙⲁ-ⲛ-ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'place of assembly' + ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'inward.' Synonym for the function the sea performs as πανδοχεῖον.
Translated 'abiding-rains' as ⲙⲟⲩⲛ ('abide, continue') + ϩⲱⲟⲩ ('rain'). The continuous/abiding rains that pour down from above into the sea.

'Shall blow it forth and draw it to himself.' ⲛⲉϥⲧϥ from ⲛⲓϥⲉ 'blow/breathe' with object suffix; ⲥⲁⲕϥ̄ from ⲥⲱⲕ 'draw' with object suffix; ⲛⲉϥ = 'to him' (the prow). The prow's breathing-and-drawing action is the cosmological mechanism by which the sea-receptacle gathers all material.
